years.title: Machines That Guess
years.big_question: Can a machine make a guess?

lessons.title: Does it guess?
lessons.big_idea: Some machines do the same thing every time. Some make guesses, and those use AI.
lessons.activity: The Mystery Bag: everyday objects come out one at a time and the class decides "same every time" or "makes a guess".

lessons.title: Teaching Bleep
lessons.big_idea: AI learns from lots of examples.
lessons.activity: Bleep, the class robot puppet, is taught what fruit is. Two examples lead to silly guesses; many varied examples make Bleep better.

lessons.title: The Mystery Rule
lessons.big_idea: AI spots patterns, then guesses. Meet the AI Loop.
lessons.activity: The teacher sorts objects into two hoops using a secret rule; the class learns, spots, guesses and checks, then pupils invent rules for each other.

lessons.title: Why did it show me that?
lessons.big_idea: Some AI chooses what we see next.
lessons.activity: Bleep's Video Shelf: the cards children pick change what Bleep puts on the "up next" shelf, until the shelf only shows one thing.

lessons.title: Picture this
lessons.big_idea: AI can make pictures from our words, but people choose the words.
lessons.activity: The class designs a picture in words, the teacher creates it with a school approved tool, and pupils compare it with their own drawings: who made which?

lessons.title: Boss of the Bot
lessons.big_idea: People make AI and people are in charge.
lessons.activity: Pupils design jobs for a classroom helper robot, decide what only people should do and what we never tell a machine, and write the class Robot Rules.

years.title: Using AI Wisely
years.big_question: How do we stay in charge of AI?

lessons.title: Check it!
lessons.big_idea: AI guesses can be wrong, so people check.
lessons.activity: Check It paddles: Bleep labels pictures (a muffin becomes a puppy) and pupils catch and fix the mistakes.

lessons.title: Missing examples
lessons.big_idea: When examples are missing, AI gets things wrong for some people and things.
lessons.activity: Build a Bird: groups teach a partner what a bird is from a card pack, then test with a penguin, an ostrich and a kiwi to see whose pack let them down.

lessons.title: Try it first
lessons.big_idea: My brain grows when I do the hard thinking.
lessons.activity: Helper or Doer? Bleep keeps offering to finish pupils' puzzles; the class discovers what they lose when Bleep does it, and when Bleep's help is useful.

lessons.title: Keep it to yourself
lessons.big_idea: Some things we never tell a machine.
lessons.activity: Bleep Wants to Know: Bleep asks friendly questions and pupils sort them into Safe to Say and Keep to Myself, then practise what to do.

lessons.title: AI Helpers Hall of Fame
lessons.big_idea: AI helps people in homes, hospitals, farms and streets.
lessons.activity: Pupils meet real AI helpers through picture cards and vote them into a class Hall of Fame, explaining what each one guesses and who checks it.

lessons.title: Bleep's Big Day Out
lessons.big_idea: Using everything we know.
lessons.activity: Bleep joins a class trip told as a story; at each stop pupils decide how to keep Bleep in check, keep information private and use Bleep on purpose.

years.title: AI in Everyday Life
years.big_question: Where is AI in my life, and is it helping?

lessons.title: What's in your feed?
lessons.big_idea: Apps learn from what we do, then choose what we see.
lessons.activity: The Feed Machine: the class acts as a video app that learns from every like, and watches its feed shrink into a bubble.

lessons.title: Is it always listening?
lessons.big_idea: Voice assistants collect information about us.
lessons.activity: Wake Word: pupils play a voice assistant listening for its name, discover what it hears along the way, and decide what should stay private.

lessons.title: AI that helps everyone
lessons.big_idea: AI can open doors for people who see, hear or speak differently.
lessons.activity: Access stations: pupils meet everyday barriers, then see how captions, read aloud, translation and describing apps remove them, including a round trip translation test.

lessons.title: Hint, not answer
lessons.big_idea: The best help makes you think.
lessons.activity: Helper Cards: pupils rank different kinds of help from "thinks for me" to "makes me think", then write hint questions for a partner.

lessons.title: Who made it?
lessons.big_idea: Being honest about when AI has helped.
lessons.activity: Dear Bleep: Bleep writes for advice on tricky situations about schoolwork, art and stories; pupils reply and design a "Made with AI" label.

lessons.title: The Helpful Feed
lessons.big_idea: Designing technology that is good for children.
lessons.activity: Teams redesign a children's video app: a "why am I seeing this?" button, healthy limits, clear AI labels, no personal data. They pitch their design to the class.

years.title: Machines That Talk
years.big_question: Do chatbots know what they are saying?

lessons.title: What comes next?
lessons.big_idea: Chatbots build answers by predicting the next word.
lessons.activity: The Word Chain Machine: pupils tally which words follow which in a class story, then roll dice to generate sentences that sound right but can be nonsense.

lessons.title: Is a chatbot a friend?
lessons.big_idea: Chatbots can sound friendly but do not know or care about you.
lessons.activity: Two Replies: compare a chatbot reply and a friend's reply to the same message, then make a Helping Hand of trusted people.

lessons.title: Sure isn't right
lessons.big_idea: Chatbots can sound certain and still be wrong.
lessons.activity: Chatty's Quiz Show: teams decide Trust it, Test it or Bin it for confident claims, then test them with magnets, spoons, atlases and books.

lessons.title: Ask it better
lessons.big_idea: What you ask shapes what you get.
lessons.activity: Prompt Chef: pupils give a partner instructions to draw a creature, discover what vague instructions produce, and rewrite them to be specific.

lessons.title: How sure is it?
lessons.big_idea: AI does not know things; it works out what is most likely.
lessons.activity: Chance Machine: spinners and weather forecasts lead to a class guessing game with confidence scores, showing why 90% sure can still be wrong.

lessons.title: Chatty's Rulebook
lessons.big_idea: What would a good chatbot for children do?
lessons.activity: Teams write the rules a children's chatbot must follow: say when unsure, never pretend to be a friend, point to trusted adults, protect privacy. Then they test each other's rules with tricky messages.

years.title: Data, Training and Fairness
years.big_question: Where does AI learn from, and is it fair?

lessons.title: Rules or examples?
lessons.big_idea: Some programs follow rules we write; AI learns from examples.
lessons.activity: Pupils write a rule-based sorting program in Scratch, then try to beat it with tricky cases a trained model would handle, and vice versa.

lessons.title: Train the sorter
lessons.big_idea: AI is trained on one set of data and tested on another.
lessons.activity: Zorbs and Glims: teams write rules from labelled creature cards, test them on unseen cards and score their accuracy out of ten.

lessons.title: Whose is it anyway?
lessons.big_idea: Training data comes from people's work and lives, so permission matters.
lessons.activity: The Robot Art Company collects pupils' drawings without asking; the class unpicks how that felt and writes a Permission Charter.

lessons.title: The Welcome Bot
lessons.big_idea: Unbalanced data leads to unfair results.
lessons.activity: With a budget of twelve voice samples, teams choose who to train a school Welcome Bot on, then test it on visitors to see who it fails.

lessons.title: Climb the STAIR
lessons.big_idea: Using AI to help you learn, not to learn for you.
lessons.activity: Pupils plan a learning goal, write STAIR prompts that ask AI to quiz them or give feedback rather than answers, see them run in a teacher demonstration, then explain what they learned without the tool.

lessons.title: Train a class model
lessons.big_idea: Building, testing and improving a real AI model.
lessons.activity: Teacher-led, with no pupil accounts: the class trains an image model to sort recycling, tests it fairly, finds where it fails and improves the data.

years.title: AI, Society and the Future
years.big_question: Who decides how AI is used?

lessons.title: Real or generated?
lessons.big_idea: AI can fake images, voices and video, so we need a checking routine and firm rules about real people.
lessons.activity: The Gallery of Fakes: pupils hunt for clues, build the class Pause, Look, Ask, Check routine and agree why we never make or share AI images of real people without consent.

lessons.title: Who's missing from the picture?
lessons.big_idea: AI can repeat and magnify the patterns, and the unfairness, in its data.
lessons.activity: Draw, Tally, Compare: pupils quickly draw "a scientist", tally their own results, compare them with what image generators tend to produce, then fix the recipe.

lessons.title: AI at work
lessons.big_idea: AI is changing jobs, and some things stay human.
lessons.activity: Job Swap Shop: pupils sort the tasks in real jobs into "AI could help", "AI could do" and "needs a person", then invent a job of the future.

lessons.title: Is it worth it?
lessons.big_idea: AI uses energy, water and materials, and can also help the planet.
lessons.activity: Power Tokens: teams plan a class project on a limited energy budget, deciding where AI is worth its cost, and write a Planet Promise.

lessons.title: Who's responsible?
lessons.big_idea: When AI makes a decision, people must be able to explain it and answer for it.
lessons.activity: The Investigation: when an automatic line calling system at a tennis tournament fails, pupils interview the people involved, decide who is responsible and write recommendations.

lessons.title: AI for Good Design Studio
lessons.big_idea: Designing AI that helps people.
lessons.activity: Teams scope a real problem in school or the community, design an AI helper using the AI Loop, run an IDEAL audit, pitch to a panel, and each pupil writes an AI learning promise for secondary school.
